frames.title: Lesson 67 · be inclined to do — form

body: **Foco:** be inclined to do — forma.
**Pronúncia:** Ênfase intencional.
**22 palavras novas** (comunicação intercultural).
**Texto do dia:** notícia / reportagem curta.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C1):** eu consigo usar be inclined to, tend to, be apt to e be prone to para falar de tendências e disposições numa notícia intercultural.

body: Esta aula treina **ler textos curtos e achar informação (IELTS Reading, TOEFL Reading)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.headline: Survey: Teams Are Inclined to Avoid Open Conflict
paras: A new survey of 800 multinational teams suggests that members **are inclined to** avoid open conflict. Managers **tend to** interpret silence as agreement, and employees **are apt to** postpone disagreements. Teams with mixed cultures **are prone to** misunderstanding, **but are inclined to** repair it quickly when trust exists.
Researchers **are less inclined to** blame culture alone; personality, they say, **tends to** matter as much.

blocks.body: **prone to** costuma ter conotação **negativa** (accident-prone, prone to error). **Inclined to** é mais neutro e indica **opinião ou disposição**.

items.label: Ênfase intencional
items.note: A ênfase intencional destaca a palavra que carrega o sentido: sílaba forte, mais longa e mais alta. Mudar a palavra enfatizada muda a mensagem.
words: I didn’t say HE stole it.
I didn’t SAY he stole it.
Not only did she COME, she LED.

blocks.task: Write 6 sentences about team behavior using be inclined to, tend to, be apt to and be prone to.
blocks.model: Teams are inclined to avoid open conflict. Managers tend to interpret silence as agreement. Employees are apt to postpone disagreements. Mixed-culture teams are prone to misunderstanding. They are inclined to repair it quickly when trust exists. Researchers are less inclined to blame culture alone.
